task: Find the latest article regarding the economic implications of climate change in Europe as reported by BBC News and summarize the central points.
answer: Latest BBC News article on the economic implications of climate change in Europe: 'Spain battles climate change on several fronts' (published 22 September 2026, BBC News, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwg59g3vz564o). Central points: (1) Record wildfires, made ~40x more likely by global warming, burned ~300,000 hectares in Spain this year - about half the EU total - destroying farmland, livestock and hay. (2) Agriculture hit hard: Agroseguro estimates 16,000 hectares of crops destroyed by mid-August, a major blow to the agri-food industry (9% of Spain's GDP); state compensation covers less than half farmers' losses. (3) Tourism (13% of GDP) at risk: a record 61 heatwave days deter visitors, cutting overnight stays and arrivals, shifting the season to spring/autumn and spurring 'coolcation' travel. (4) Drought forced Catalonia to cut industrial water use 25% and crop farming 80% in 2024, damaging the local economy. (5) The Oct 2024 Valencia floods killed 237 people and caused an estimated €4.5bn in direct damage, affecting thousands of businesses. (6) Spain is ranked the 20th most climate-affected country (Germanwatch); economists (BBVA Research) warn heat drags down productivity and growth unless a greener economy turns the crisis into an opportunity.
